# mulib-geom-deform

<!-- Generated by tools/media_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Geometry  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

Twist, taper and cylindrical bend point deformation.

The scope above is the implemented baseline, not a claim of complete format, numerical, security or application conformance.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

twist uses radians per Z length, taper uses scale slope per Z length, and bend curvature has inverse-length units. These pointwise functions do not update normals, indices or bounding structures.

Control points and output positions use double-precision vec3 values in caller-selected length units. Parameters, weights and knots are scalars. Arrays and callback contexts are borrowed; output mesh capacities count vertices and triangles, not bytes. Supply finite inputs; these are approximate numerical operations, not exact CAD.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../kernels/mulib-geom-deform.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_geom_deform_twist(mulib_mesh_vec3 p,double radians_per_z);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_geom_deform_taper(mulib_mesh_vec3 p,double slope);
static inline mulib_mesh_vec3 mulib_geom_deform_bend(mulib_mesh_vec3 p,double k);
```

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/media-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/media-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/media-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_media.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
